productTerms.save (to device): enregistrer — but never alone on a button: in the Pinterest app « Enregistrer » means pin to a board
productTerms.pin: épingle (UI); 'pin' acceptable as a search synonym only
productTerms.GIF pin: épingle GIF (GIF is masculine: « un GIF »)
productTerms.profile picture / PFP / DP: photo de profil ; slang « pp » (FR) ; 'DP' is not used in French
productTerms.link / URL: lien (preferred), URL acceptable; short link = lien court (pin.it)
productTerms.no watermark: sans logo ajouté (users type 'sans logo' / 'sans watermark'; 'filigrane' is correct French but not searched)
productTerms.bookmarklet: favori (Chrome: « Favoris », « barre de favoris »); Firefox: marque-page; Safari and Québec: signet. Write « favori (bookmarklet) » once, then « favori ».
PintDownload n’est pas affilié à Pinterest Inc. (service indépendant)

claimTicketMetaphor.concept: A Pinterest link is a claim ticket, the file is collected at the counter. French has an exact everyday frame: the coat-check / left-luggage « ticket de vestiaire », « contremarque », and « à retirer » (what you collect at a counter: « commande à retirer »). Use that vocabulary in labels; never in body copy where clarity matters.
claimTicketMetaphor.claim ticket: ticket (le ticket) / ticket de retrait; « contremarque » is precise but formal — use in microcopy at most once
claimTicketMetaphor.Admit one · public link: « Entrée · lien public » (129px vs 153px EN at label size). Alternative with stronger voucher flavour: « Bon pour un fichier · lien public » (217px; check the ticket header fits next to the serial on 320px screens).
claimTicketMetaphor.No. (serial): N° (U+00B0 is in the font) — « N° 1120271… »
claimTicketMetaphor.stub (tear-off): talon (talon de ticket); perforation = pointillés (« détachez suivant les pointillés »)
claimTicketMetaphor.Ready · <kind> (receipt band): « À retirer · Épingle vidéo », « À retirer · Carrousel », « À retirer · Tableau », « À retirer · Photo de profil ». 'À retirer' avoids gender agreement problems of 'Prêt/Prête'.
claimTicketMetaphor.Collect button: do NOT use « Retirer » on a button (also means 'remove'); use the action: « Télécharger le MP4 », « Télécharger l’image », « Télécharger le ZIP »

stub labels.Download Image: Télécharger l’image (same words as Pinterest’s own button)
stub labels.Get Profile Picture (HD): Photo de profil HD (the literal « Obtenir la photo de profil (HD) » measures 353px at stub size and will not fit a 343px phone ticket)

stamps.Void: Annulé (what real French tickets are stamped)

claimTicketMetaphor.Saves as: Enregistré sous (echoes the OS « Enregistrer sous »)
claimTicketMetaphor.Trim sound: Découper l’audio — NOT « Couper le son » (that means 'mute')
claimTicketMetaphor.Packing n of N files…: Préparation du ZIP : n sur N fichiers…
claimTicketMetaphor.Wrong-link help: « Ce n’est pas un lien Pinterest. Dans l’appli, touchez l’icône de partage puis « Copier le lien », et collez-le ici. »

glossary.register: Vouvoiement (« Collez le lien… »), the default for FR/BE/CA/Africa. Publer uses 'tu'; it reads too casual for Belgium/Africa and for a utility that handles rights questions.

formats.numbers: Decimal comma (1,5 Mo). Thousands separator: non-breaking space (12 400 épingles; U+00A0 in display type, U+202F allowed in system-font body). Resolutions stay as labels without spaces: 720p, 1080p, 4K. Dimensions: 1080 × 1920 (U+00D7, in the font).
formats.fileSizes: Ko, Mo, Go (octets) — never KB/MB/GB. Same in Québec (OQLF).
formats.dates: Long form « 14 octobre 2026 » (lowercase month) works in every market; avoid numeric dates because France/Belgium use 14/10/2026 and Québec prefers 2026-10-14. Serial strip in uppercase gothic: « 14 OCT. 2026 ».
formats.punctuation: Non-breaking space before : ; ? ! and inside « guillemets » (France/Belgium norm). Big Shoulders lacks U+202F (narrow nbsp), so use U+00A0 in headings, labels, <title> and meta. Québec typography drops the space before ; ? ! — one shared French version with the France norm is acceptable there. Typographic apostrophe ’ (U+2019) in copy; slugs drop it.
formats.currency: Not shown (free). JSON-LD offers price '0' can keep priceCurrency as is; EUR is fine for the fr version.
formats.openGraph: og:locale fr_FR (OG requires language_TERRITORY) with og:locale:alternate en_US; html lang="fr"; JSON-LD inLanguage "fr".

typography.glyphCoverage: Checked the shipped woff2 subsets (public/fonts/big-shoulders-display-latin-800/900-normal.woff2): all French letters present (É È Ê Ë À Â Ç Î Ï Ô Ù Û Ü Œ œ Æ « » ’ … × ° €). Missing: Ÿ (only in rare proper nouns), U+202F narrow nbsp, and → (U+2192, already used by English stamps; falls back to Arial Narrow).
typography.uppercaseAccents: French keeps accents on capitals (« TÉLÉCHARGER », « À RETIRER »). CSS text-transform: uppercase does this correctly as long as the page has lang="fr"; never hand-type unaccented capitals.
typography.lineHeightRisk: In the 900 weight, É/À/Ê/Ô/Î reach 0.979–0.980 em above the baseline (plain E: 0.80 em). With the display line-height of 0.88–0.90, an accented capital on line 2 rises 0.08–0.10 em into line 1's baseline zone, and on line 1 it pokes about 0.14 em above the line box (clipping risk under overflow:hidden, or touching breadcrumbs). Recommendation: :lang(fr) .t-display / H1 / headline line-height 1.0 (or ≥0.98) plus padding-top 0.1em; re-measure the desktop seam alignment (H1 cap line vs ticket top) after the change.
typography.lengthExpansion: Measured with the shipped 900 woff2 glyph advances (uppercase, -0.01em tracking, greedy word wrap; mobile = 46px type in a 343px column, i.e. 375px minus two 16px gutters; desktop = 60px type in an estimated 472px copy column at 1024px). French H1 widths run from -18% to +30% vs English. The first drafts of the photo, MP3 and MP4 H1s added a line, so they were shortened. Final set: no French H1 needs more lines than its English counterpart, and two need fewer (photo de profil 3→2, 4K desktop 3→2). The longest word, TÉLÉCHARGEUR, is 244px at 46px, so no word overflows a 320px phone; no hyphenation needed in headings (keep hyphens: manual on display type; hyphens:auto is fine in body copy with lang=fr).
typography.labelsAndStub: Labels (0.875rem, 0.08em): FR band labels grow ~+45% (« À RETIRER · ÉPINGLE VIDÉO » 161px vs 111px) — fine in the band but check the right-hand serial does not collide on 320px. Stub (1.625rem): « TÉLÉCHARGER LA VIDÉO » 239px vs 185px — fits; avoid the literal PFP label (353px).

ticketHeaderAlt.fr: Bon pour un fichier · lien public

notes: One French version for every market. Google autocomplete with hl=fr is nearly identical across gl=fr, ca and be (117 seeds each; ca differed on 9 seeds, be on 10, and only by an extra tail suggestion). The Côte d'Ivoire, Senegal and Cameroon checks (55 seeds each, 7 intents; differences on 6–8 seeds, all in the generic and video tails) showed the same pattern plus more app-install and 'haute qualité' / 'sur telephone' tails. Separate fr-CA/fr-BE pages would be duplicates.

URL scheme: /fr + localized ASCII slugs (canonical without trailing slash, so the French home is https://pintdownload.app/fr, which matches hostRedirectUrl/normalizeCanonical). Klickpin/SavePin/ScreenApp keep English slugs under /fr/; Metricool, which ranks for the how-to queries, uses French slugs. Localized slugs echo the query and make better French anchor text.

Each French page: self-referencing canonical; reciprocal hreflang fr ↔ en plus x-default → English on both sides; html lang="fr"; server-rendered French (not the current client-side i18n.ts swap); French FAQPage/HowTo JSON-LD (no aggregateRating); breadcrumb 'Accueil' → /fr (BaseLayout hardcodes 'Home' and splits the title on '—', so French titles use ' — ' with the page name first); French alt text on every img; sitemap entries for the 15 French URLs with xhtml:link alternates.

Skipped pages (profile, carousel, story, SEO title generator) get no fr alternate. Their English pages keep hreflang en + x-default only. French pages must not link to them with French anchor text that suggests a French page: label such links « (en anglais) » or route them to the French page that covers the intent (carousel → épingle, profile → tableau FAQ, story → vidéo FAQ).

Cannibalization map (keep distinct intents, interlink): tool 'télécharger vidéo pinterest' (transactional) vs 'convertisseur pinterest mp4' (converter wording) vs 'comment télécharger une vidéo pinterest' (method hub) vs 'enregistrer … dans sa galerie' (Android/Samsung) vs 'iPhone' vs 'PC'. The English 'how-to … to Gallery' title must not be copied: in French it would compete with the galerie page.

Mixed intent on 'télécharger pinterest': many searchers want the official app (apk, pc, mac, windows, lite, 'gratuit français'). Don't target app-install terms. Add one honest FAQ on the home page pointing to the official App Store / Google Play listings, and never offer or link an APK.

Accents: people often type without accents ('telecharger video pinterest'). Google folds accents, so write correct French with accents everywhere; never strip them to match queries (SavePin does, and it reads as broken French). Slugs are ASCII by rule.

Honesty carry-over risks in the English sources: pinterest-4k-downloader claims '4K ultra quality' and 'original uncompressed'; pinterest-profile-picture-downloader says 'full-resolution uncropped'; pinterest-seo-title-generator states an unsourced 'up to 40%' click-through stat and '100% free with unlimited generations'. The French copy must not translate these. The video quality line ('souvent 720p ou 1080p') mirrors the English FAQ and should be checked against what /api/extract actually returns before launch.

Pinterest's own download button: the French help center documents « Télécharger l’image » for images, and the mobile ⋯ menu shows « Télécharger ». Video download only appears when the creator allows it. The how-to guide should say this before recommending PintDownload; it is honest and it matches the top French SERP framing (BDM: « Peut-on télécharger une vidéo sur Pinterest ? »).

Legal FAQ framing for French markets: droit d’auteur plus droit à l’image (France: art. 9 du Code civil), most relevant on the photo-de-profil page. Keep it to plain guidance (« usage personnel, demandez l’accord, créditez »), not legal advice. Say « PintDownload n’est pas affilié à Pinterest Inc. » in the footer and in the first FAQ answer.

Data-light markets (Francophone Africa: 'pinterest lite' and Android/apk queries are prominent): the French pages should stay as light as the English ones. Don't add French-only fonts or large images; the existing latin woff2 subset already covers French.

The client-side i18n.ts French strings need a rewrite before reuse: heroSubtitle promises « qualité Full HD 1080p » for everything (photos and boards aren't 1080p video), and the labels are generic. Treat the glossary above as the source for French UI strings.

Native review: copy was drafted for fr-FR and checked against query wording and Pinterest's French UI labels. Have a native French speaker proofread before launch (ideally one familiar with Québec usage).

Validation: all 15 titles (55–62 chars) and descriptions (149–157 chars) are counted in Unicode code points, as seo_health_check.py counts them. Synthetic pages built from these values pass the repo's check_html_file() with 0 errors and 0 warnings.
